metadata.note: The original 1949-1970 California Zephyr and its Exposition Flyer predecessor, jointly operated by three railroads. Note this ran the Western Pacific's Feather River Canyon route west of Winnemucca, a different alignment from Amtrak's modern California Zephyr over Donner Pass. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; any place where the historical routing differed is described in the segment notes and reflected in the geometry. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones (train introductions, renamings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (California Zephyr 1949-1970, Exposition Flyer), american-rails.com, calzephyr.railfan.net; https://www.wplives.org/modeling_material/WP_Mile_Post_System.pdf (Western Pacific Railroad Mile Post System: exact mileposts and station/siding names for the full Oakland-Stockton line, First Subdivision, including Oakland Yard 4.70, Oakland 6.57, Fruitvale 9.60, San Leandro 14.80, Hayward 20.11, Carpenter 24.90, Union City 25.88, Decoto 26.46, Pabrico 27.80, Eberly 28.90, Fremont 29.70, Niles Junction 30.50, Hearst 38.08, Pleasanton 41.66, Radum 42.70-43.34, Livermore Team Track 47.05, Altamont 56.17, Midway 63.34, Tracy 72.79, Wyche 82.14, Stockton 93.78); OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API) active-rail geometry for the Stockton-Wyche-Tracy-Midway-Altamont-Livermore-Radum-Pleasanton-Sunol-Niles Junction-Niles-Fremont-Decoto-Hayward-San Leandro-Fruitvale-Oakland stretch, routed via Dijkstra shortest path with no straight-line fallbacks needed anywhere on this stretch
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The original California Zephyr began Mar 20 1949, jointly run by the CB&Q (Chicago-Denver), Rio Grande (Denver-Salt Lake City) and Western Pacific (Salt Lake City-Oakland), scheduled so passengers passed the best scenery in daylight. West of Winnemucca it ran Western Pacific's Feather River Canyon route via Portola and Oroville, then over Altamont Pass via Pleasanton - not the Donner Pass route Amtrak's California Zephyr uses today - and this geometry follows that historical Feather River alignment. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: Western Pacific applied to drop its portion in 1966 and the ICC refused after public outcry; the Rio Grande applied in 1969, and in 1970 the ICC finally let Western Pacific end its portion, killing the original train. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The Rio Grande stayed out of Amtrak and ran its own Rio Grande Zephyr, Denver-Salt Lake City, with the original equipment until 1983. Amtrak revived the California Zephyr name on the Donner Pass routing - see amtrak.geojson. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
